value.hook: Open before writing code that ends, prunes or nudges something on a seat's behalf (delivered, release, prune, idle nudges), or picking up plan 224
value.title: wildcat: holdings that end themselves, prune and prime, and how reviewers break them

sections.name: body
sections.value:
Lessons from #168 (plan 215), #170 (F107 prune), #177 (F119/F117) and #186 (F122), all merged, each after 2 to 4 review rounds.

1. Anything that ends a holding later than the work finished needs two guards, and reviewers will find the second one missing.
   - Bind the release to the work: plan 215 ends only holdings whose `from` is before the PR's mergedAt (from the same gh read).
   - Pin identity across the lock gap: selection reads the store outside the writer lock, so ReleaseTarget carries `from`, and release_many ends a target only if that exact holding is still open.
   - Test the pin with a two-phase test: finished_by, then inject a release and reassign, then release_many. No timing.
2. Delivered keys: reviewer/security/performance/<pr>; coder/<plan> from the docs/plans scan; coder/f<N> from a strict `Fixes: F1, F2` body line (no line, no guess; a malformed line refuses E-RS-FIXES before the record, and the CI delivers check fails it first).
   - Open proof gap from spoonbill: the malformed-Fixes test uses a `Delivers: none` body, so it can't show nothing was recorded. Add a real Delivers address if someone touches it.
3. Destructive sweeps (pr-freeze --prune) must fail closed on every observation.
   - Decides: the PR state, validated (MERGED, CLOSED, or OPEN with a 40-hex head).
   - Brakes, which only spare: any git status stderr, a seat folder or lsof cwd inside the worktree, an unresolvable path.
   - Refuse with no removals on: lsof nonzero exit, stderr, an unparsed record, a pid with no cwd; a malformed seat row; any child timeout; a warning on the worktree list or seat list.
   - It's macOS only: Linux /proc can't prove absence.
   - Resolve git, gh and pij-rs to absolute paths once per run.
4. The prime is designated (project prime_id), never assigned (C24). Legacy prime assignment rows count for nothing: not liveness, not idle activity, not actions. Gate prime recovery on the designation's own liveness. assign prime refuses E-RS-DIRECTORY-PRIME-DESIGNATED.
5. Process.
   - Two guards that cover for each other make single mutants survive: test each layer directly.
   - Run mutants on a scratch copy (cp backup, restore), never commit them.
   - Main moves often: re-check `merge-base --is-ancestor` right before push, and re-gate after every main merge.
   - A `&&` chain that fails silently skips the push: verify with `git ls-remote`.
